items.title: Alvin Alcorn Interview, 1976-01-25
items.q: Nina had quit, but Monk Hazel, there wasn't anything else to do.

ctx.x: Maybe we can do another reel, huh? And talk about Mississippi musicians. Of course, I want to talk about a lot of people. Like where Bert Sigerson is now. To find him, you reminded me of that. What Sidney Ayrton used to call a BAME system clarinet, what he called an ALBA system. Yeah. What did you say it was?

Well, Sidney referred to the ALBA system clarinet as a few key. He referred to the BAME system clarinet, which had so many more keys, as a thousand-legged clarinet. And, of course, Sidney was extremely interesting to me. And he played in South Louisiana with a little dance down there for years. He played with Joe Rivette. And Joe Rivette was very famous to that part of Louisiana in the 30s. Sidney, well, they used to have a little slogan, it's a swingin' sweat with Joe Rivette. He later became a gambler, a…

I swear I heard... Excuse me, go ahead. That's where I interviewed Jack and where I interviewed Noxy. No kidding. Yeah. You know, and eventually the name of it changed. And it eventually became one of these banjo places your father's playing.
